recipes.name: Pasta Fresca all'Uovo (Fresh Egg Pasta)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, supple sheets with a rich golden colour and a gentle eggy sweetness, tender but with a little bite once cooked.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein, choline and vitamin B12 to the flour, so a plate of fresh egg pasta carries more protein than one made with water alone.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
ingredients.cutPrep: tipo 00 soft wheat flour, plus a little for dusting
ingredients.prepNote: Italian 00 flour is the usual choice; all purpose flour is the nearest match in the database
about one egg for every 100 g of flour

instructions: Heap the flour on a wooden board and make a wide well in the middle.
Break the eggs into the well and beat them with a fork, drawing in flour from the inside wall a little at a time.
When the dough is too stiff for the fork, bring it together with your hands and a bench scraper.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes, pushing away with the heel of the hand and folding back, until smooth and elastic; add a pinch of flour if it sticks or a few drops of water if it cracks.
Wrap the dough and rest it at room temperature for 30 to 60 minutes so the gluten relaxes.
Roll it out with a long pin or a pasta machine, keeping the rest covered, to about 1 mm for filled pasta and 1 to 1.5 mm for tagliatelle, then cut or fill as the dish asks.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs and the wheat flour.

citations.source: Ricette dal Mondo, Pasta fresca all'uovo
Visit Tuscany, La ricetta della pasta fresca all'uovo

recipes.curationNote: Both sources use one egg per 100 g of flour (400 g with 4 eggs, 500 g with 5) and a rest of at least 30 minutes; kept the 400 g batch. One serving is the dough from 100 g of flour, about 160 g of fresh pasta, a plate for one. Tagliatelle, lasagne, tortellini, ravioli, cannelloni and agnolotti all point here.

recipes.name: Pasta di Semola (Durum Wheat Pasta Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: Firm, pale yellow dough that cooks up chewy and rough, so sauce clings to every ridge.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made only from durum semolina and water, it is egg free and gives steady carbohydrate with a fair amount of protein from the hard wheat.

ingredients.cutPrep: semola rimacinata (twice milled), plus a little for dusting

ingredients.prepNote: added a little at a time, since semola varies in how much it takes
a pinch; many Pugliese cooks leave it out

instructions: Heap the semola on a board, make a well and pour in about half the lukewarm water with the salt.
Work the water in with your fingers, then add the rest a little at a time until a firm, rough dough forms.
Knead for 10 to 15 minutes until smooth and compact; it should feel stiffer than egg pasta, as it softens while it rests.
Wrap and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Cut off a piece at a time, keeping the rest covered, and roll it into ropes about 1 cm thick for orecchiette or cavatelli, thinner for busiate.
Shape on a board dusted with semola and leave the pasta to dry for 30 minutes to 2 hours before cooking.

nutritionHighlights.note: Durum wheat is higher in protein than soft wheat.
A modest amount from the whole semolina.

citations.source: Ricette dal Mondo, Pasta fresca di semola

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy uses 300 g semola to 160 ml water with a little salt; Ricette dal Mondo 400 g to 240 ml with a spoon of oil. Kept water only, no oil, as Pugliese and Sicilian cooks make it, at about 52% hydration. One serving is the dough from 100 g of semola. Orecchiette, busiate and other hand-shaped pastas point here.

recipes.name: Gnocchi di Patate
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, light little dumplings that taste of potato, with a pillowy middle and a faint chew from the flour.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium and vitamin C to these, and keeping the flour low makes them lighter and closer to the potato itself.

ingredients.prepNote: older, floury potatoes need less flour

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
ingredients.cutPrep: tipo 00 flour, plus a little for the board
ingredients.prepNote: no more than one third of the potato weight

instructions: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 25 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and peel them while still hot, then pass them through a potato ricer onto a floured board and let the steam escape for 5 to 10 minutes.
Scatter over most of the flour and the salt and work it in lightly with your fingertips, just until a soft dough forms; add the rest only if it sticks.
Cut the dough into pieces and roll each into a rope about 2 cm thick, then cut into 2 cm lengths.
Roll each piece over the back of a fork or a gnocchi board to make ridges, and lay them on a floured tray without touching.
Cook in plenty of salted boiling water and lift them out with a slotted spoon 1 to 2 minutes after they rise to the surface.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potatoes, though some is lost in boiling.

recipes.curationNote: Misya uses 600 g potatoes to 200 to 250 g flour with no egg; Cookist gives the rule of no more than a third of the potato weight in flour and no egg; Recipes from Italy adds one egg. Kept the eggless version most northern cooks hold to, at 1 kg potatoes to 300 g flour. One serving is a plate for one, about 300 g of uncooked gnocchi.

recipes.name: Impasto per Pizza Napoletana
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, airy dough with a light tang from the long rise, baking up to a puffed, leopard-spotted rim and a thin, tender middle.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain dough of flour, water, salt and a little yeast; the long, slow rise is what makes it easy to digest, and the salt is worth knowing about for anyone watching sodium.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
ingredients.cutPrep: tipo 00 flour, plus a little for the board
ingredients.prepNote: Neapolitan pizzaioli use a strong 00; all purpose is the nearest match in the database
a very small amount, for a rise of 8 hours or more

instructions: Dissolve the salt in the water in a large bowl, then add about a tenth of the flour and stir.
Crumble in the yeast, then add the rest of the flour a handful at a time, mixing until the dough comes together.
Knead on the board for 10 to 20 minutes until smooth, soft and slightly tacky, then cover and rest for 2 hours at room temperature.
Divide into 6 pieces of about 260 g, shape each into a tight ball and set them in a covered tray with room between them.
Leave the balls to rise for 6 to 8 hours at about 23°C (73°F), or longer in a cool room, until soft and doubled.
Open each ball by hand, pressing from the middle outwards and leaving a 1 to 2 cm rim; never use a rolling pin.

A wood oven bakes it at 430 to 485°C (805 to 905°F) in 60 to 90 seconds; at home, bake on a stone or steel heated for 45 minutes at the oven's top heat, 250 to 290°C (480 to 550°F), for 6 to 9 minutes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt in the dough.
A modest amount from the wheat.

citations.source: Il Fatto Alimentare, Pizza napoletana: il disciplinare

recipes.curationNote: The disciplinare reported by Il Fatto Alimentare allows only 00 flour, water, salt and yeast, dough balls of 180 to 250 g, a rise of at least 8 hours and a bake of 60 to 90 seconds at 430 to 485°C. Recipes from Italy gives the home oven version. Kept a home batch of 1 kg flour to 600 ml water (60% hydration) with very little yeast for a long rise. One serving is one dough ball, about 260 g, one pizza.

recipes.name: Impasto per Focaccia
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, open crumb under a golden crust pocked with dimples, salty and slick with olive oil on top and crisp underneath.
recipes.healthBenefit: Olive oil gives this bread its fat, mostly monounsaturated; it is still a bread rich in oil and salt, best as part of a meal.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour
Leavening agents, yeast, baker's, active dry

ingredients.prepNote: or barley malt, to feed the yeast and colour the crust
for the pan and the salamoia
for the salamoia, the brine poured over before baking

instructions: Stir the yeast and honey into the lukewarm water and leave for 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the two flours in a bowl, pour in the yeast water and mix, then add the 25 ml of oil and the fine salt and knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1 to 2 hours, until doubled.
Oil a 30 x 40 cm (12 x 16 inch) baking pan, stretch the dough into it with oiled fingers, cover and rest 30 minutes, then stretch it again to the corners.
Leave to rise again for 30 to 60 minutes until puffy.
Whisk the 100 ml of water with the rest of the oil, press deep dimples all over the dough with your fingertips, pour the salamoia over so it pools in the holes and scatter the coarse salt.
Rest 20 to 30 minutes more, then bake at 230°C (445°F) for 15 to 20 minutes, until golden on top and crisp underneath.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil.
From the salt in the dough and on top.

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy uses 200 g 00 and 300 g bread flour, 300 ml water, honey, dry yeast, a brine of 100 ml water and 50 ml oil, 230°C for 15 minutes; Misya uses the same salamoia method with fresh yeast and malt. Kept Recipes from Italy quantities, which fill one 30 x 40 cm pan. One serving is one slice, an eighth of the pan.

recipes.name: Pasta Frolla
recipes.flavorProfile: Buttery, crumbly shortcrust with a scent of lemon and vanilla that bakes into a crisp, sandy, gently sweet shell.
recipes.healthBenefit: This is a sweet pastry rich in butter and sugar, so it is a treat; the eggs add a little protein.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: icing sugar gives a finer, more crumbly frolla
or the seeds of half a vanilla pod

instructions: Rub the cold butter into the sugar on a board or in a bowl until it looks like coarse sand.
Add the eggs, yolk, lemon zest, vanilla and salt and work them in quickly.
Add the flour all at once and bring it together with your fingertips just until no dry flour is left; do not knead, or the pastry turns tough.
Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill for 1 to 2 hours.
Roll it out between sheets of baking paper to 3 to 5 mm and line the tart pan, chilling it again for 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake at 180°C (355°F), blind with weights if it is to be filled afterwards, for 15 to 20 minutes, or with its filling for 30 to 40 minutes, until golden.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the butter, which makes up a large part of the pastry.
A little from the eggs and flour.

citations.source: Cookist, Pasta frolla: la ricetta classica

recipes.curationNote: Cookist gives the classic 2:1:1 frolla (500 g flour, 250 g butter, 250 g icing sugar, 2 eggs, lemon and vanilla, at least an hour in the fridge); Misya uses less butter and sugar with a pinch of bicarbonate. Kept the classic butter ratio with the sugar cut to 200 g and a yolk added. The batch is about 1 kg, enough for two 24 cm tart shells; one serving is a tenth, about 100 g of dough.

recipes.name: Pan di Spagna
recipes.flavorProfile: Tall, springy, pale gold sponge with a fine, dry crumb made to soak up syrup, cream or liqueur.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raised only by whisked eggs, with no butter, it is lighter in fat than most cakes but still a sweet made largely of sugar and flour.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C (340°F) and line the base of a 24 cm (9 inch) round pan with baking paper, leaving the sides ungreased so the batter can climb.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, salt and lemon zest with an electric whisk for 15 to 20 minutes, until pale, thick and about three times the volume; a ribbon falling from the whisk should sit on the surface.
Sift the flour and starch over in three parts, folding each in gently from the bottom up with a spatula so the air stays in.
Pour into the pan and bake for 35 to 45 minutes without opening the oven for the first 30, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Turn it out upside down onto a rack and leave to cool completely, at least 2 hours, before slicing it into layers.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Torta Diplomatica (Pan di Spagna)

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy uses the classic ratio of one egg to 30 g sugar and 30 g flour, whisked 15 to 20 minutes and baked at 170°C for 40 minutes; Misya adds boiling water and baking powder. Kept the classic version raised only by eggs, with part of the flour as starch, as many Italian pastry cooks do. One serving is one slice, a tenth of a 24 cm cake.

recipes.name: Crema Pasticcera
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, smooth, glossy custard that tastes of milk, egg and vanilla with a touch of lemon peel.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk and egg yolks bring calcium, protein and vitamin A; it is still a sweet filling with a fair amount of sugar.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: some cooks use flour, or half and half

ingredients.cutPrep: peel only, in wide strips without the white pith
ingredients.prepNote: taken out before the eggs go in
or a split vanilla pod warmed in the milk

instructions: Warm the milk with the lemon peel and vanilla over low heat until it steams, 5 to 8 minutes, then lift out the peel.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale, then whisk in the cornstarch until smooth.
Pour a little of the hot milk into the yolks and whisk, then pour everything back into the pan.
Cook over low to medium heat, whisking all the time, for 3 to 6 minutes, until the cream thickens and a few bubbles break on the surface.
Pour into a cold dish, press cling film onto the surface so no skin forms, and cool, then chill for at least 1 hour before using. It keeps 1 to 2 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and milk.

recipes.curationNote: Cookist uses 500 ml milk, 5 yolks, 150 g sugar and 45 g cornstarch; Misya 400 ml milk, 4 yolks, 100 g sugar and 40 g flour with a vanilla pod. Kept the Cookist ratio with sugar between the two. The batch is about 700 g; one serving is an eighth, about 85 g, enough for one slice of a filled tart.

recipes.name: Brodo di Carne
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, golden and deeply savoury, with the round meatiness of beef and capon and a faint sweetness from the vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: A long simmer of meat and bone gives a warming broth with some protein and minerals, a gentle base for soups and for the tortellini that are cooked in it.

ingredients.prepNote: bone and meat together give body
the cooked meat is served as bollito or kept for a filling
the Emilian broth for tortellini; a stewing hen works too

ingredients.cutPrep: halved, skin left on for colour
ingredients.prepNote: one half studded with the cloves

ingredients.name: juniper berries
ingredients.prepNote: optional, as in the Misya version

instructions: Put the beef, the bones and the capon in a large stockpot and cover with the cold water; starting cold draws more flavour out of the meat.
Bring it slowly to a bare simmer over medium heat, 30 to 40 minutes, skimming off the grey foam as it rises.
Add the onion with its cloves, the carrots, celery, bay leaves, juniper and peppercorns.
Keep it at a gentle tremble, never a rolling boil, for 2.5 to 3 hours, skimming now and then; lift out the capon after about 2 hours so it stays whole.
Season with the salt in the last 30 minutes, then lift out the meat and strain the broth through a fine sieve lined with damp cloth.
Cool it, chill overnight and lift off the hardened fat for a clear brodo. It keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge and 3 months frozen.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, drawn into the broth from the beef and capon.
From the shank bones and capon, which give the broth its body when cold.
From the carrots, celery and onion.

citations.source: Cookist, Brodo di carne: la ricetta

recipes.curationNote: Misya uses 1 kg of beef with bone, celery, carrot, onion, bay, juniper and peppercorns for 2 to 3 hours; Cookist uses 500 g of beef plus 300 g bones in 3 l water, cloves pushed into the onion, 3 hours. Added half a capon, as the Emilian brodo for tortellini is made, and kept both the cloves and the optional juniper. About 3 litres after straining, 12 cups. The nutrient total counts all the meat, which is mostly lifted out, so the broth itself carries less than the list suggests.

recipes.name: Brodo Vegetale
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, sweet and fresh, tasting of carrot, celery and tomato, a quiet background for risotto and soups.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made only from vegetables and water, it is vegan and low in fat, and carries some potassium from the vegetables into whatever it is cooked into.

ingredients.prepNote: or 8 to 10 cherry tomatoes, as Cookist uses
or leave it unsalted and season the dish

instructions: Wash the vegetables and cut them into large pieces so they do not break up and cloud the broth.
Put everything except the salt in a large pot with the cold water.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered, for 1.5 to 2.5 hours.
Add the salt in the last few minutes, then strain through a fine sieve without pressing the vegetables.
Use it hot for risotto or soup, or cool it and keep it 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potato, carrots, celery and tomatoes.
From the carrots and tomatoes, a small amount carried into the broth.

recipes.curationNote: Misya: zucchini, potato, 2 tomatoes, 2 carrots, 2 onions, 3 celery, garlic, parsley, peppercorns and bay in 3 l water for 1.5 hours. Cookist: 3 l water, celery, cherry tomatoes, carrots, onions and zucchini for 2.5 hours. Kept the Misya list, which takes in the Cookist one. About 2.5 litres, 10 cups. Nutrients count the whole vegetables, most of which are strained out.

recipes.name: Fumetto di Pesce
recipes.flavorProfile: Clean and briny with a soft sweetness, the taste of the sea without any heaviness.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made from fish heads and bones that would otherwise be thrown away, it brings a little protein and minerals from the sea to risotto and seafood pasta.

ingredients.name: white fish heads and bones (sea bass, sea bream, gurnard, scorpionfish)
ingredients.cutPrep: gills removed, rinsed in cold water
ingredients.prepNote: oily fish such as mackerel or sardine make it bitter
as Misya uses, for colour and sweetness

instructions: Pull the gills out of the heads, then rinse the heads and bones under cold running water until it runs clear.
Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic for 3 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the fish, stir for a minute, then add the tomatoes, parsley, bay, peppercorns and cold water.
Bring just to a simmer, skim the foam, and keep it barely moving, never a full boil, for 30 to 60 minutes.
Strain gently through a sieve lined with cloth without pressing the solids, which would cloud it. Leave it unsalted so the finished dish can be seasoned.
Keep it 2 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the fish heads and bones.

citations.source: Cookist, Fumetto di pesce: la ricetta

recipes.curationNote: Misya: 500 g fish scraps, 1 l water, oil, garlic, parsley, 5 cherry tomatoes, carrot, peppercorns, 30 minutes. Cookist: 1 kg white fish scraps, 2 l water, bay, celery, carrot, onion, never a full boil, skimmed, longer cooking. Used the Cookist quantities with the Misya tomatoes and a light sweat in oil. Fish heads and bones are not in the food database, so they are listed as not counted rather than standing in a fillet for them. About 1.5 litres, 6 cups.

recipes.name: Sugo di Pomodoro
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright, sweet and gently acidic, with garlic warmth and fresh basil, smooth enough to coat every strand.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cooked tomatoes in olive oil are a good source of lycopene, which the body takes up more easily from cooked tomato eaten with fat.

ingredients.baseName: Tomatoes, canned products, whole, without salt
ingredients.cutPrep: two tins of peeled plum tomatoes (San Marzano if you can)

ingredients.prepNote: or half an onion, finely chopped, as many home cooks use
optional, a knob stirred in at the end as Locatelli does

instructions: Put the oil and garlic in a cold wide pan and warm it gently over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the garlic smells sweet and is barely golden.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and passata, add the salt, and bring to a lively simmer.
After 5 minutes crush the tomatoes against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon.
Simmer uncovered over low to medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy; lift out the garlic.
Take it off the heat, tear in the basil and stir in the butter if using. It keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cooked tomatoes, taken up better with the olive oil.
From the tomatoes, partly kept through the short cooking.

citations.source: Ricette dal Mondo, Sugo al pomodoro
Cookist, Tutti i trucchi di Giorgio Locatelli per un sugo al pomodoro perfetto

recipes.curationNote: Ricette dal Mondo uses 400 g pulp and 700 ml passata with oil, half an onion, a pinch of sugar and basil for 20 to 25 minutes. Locatelli uses peeled tins, garlic warmed from a cold pan, crushes the tomatoes after the first simmer, no sugar and a knob of butter at the end. Kept the Locatelli method with a mix of tins and passata, no sugar. About 1.1 litres, enough for 500 g of pasta, 6 servings.

recipes.name: Ragù alla Bolognese
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, meaty and mellow, the tomato only a background to slowly cooked beef and pancetta, softened by milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good source of protein, iron and zinc from the beef, best eaten as Bologna does, a modest amount over fresh egg pasta.

components.note: hot, added a ladle at a time

ingredients.cutPrep: coarsely minced, ideally beef skirt or flank

ingredients.prepNote: or 50 g butter, both are used in Bologna
or 5 tbsp of tomato paste, as the 1982 recipe allows

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Melt the pancetta with the oil in a heavy pan over medium low heat for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Raise the heat, add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until it has lost its raw colour and starts to sizzle, 8 to 10 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble until it has evaporated, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the passata, lower the heat to the barest simmer, cover partly and cook for about 2 hours, adding hot broth a ladle at a time whenever it looks dry.
Near the end stir in the milk, simmer 10 to 15 minutes more, and season with salt and pepper. It keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well.

citations.source: Cookist, Ragù alla bolognese: la ricetta

recipes.curationNote: Followed the recipe filed by the Accademia Italiana della Cucina with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce on 17 October 1982, as both sources describe it: 300 g beef, 150 g pancetta, a small carrot, celery and onion, 300 g passata, white wine, milk, broth, about 2 hours. Cookist adds pork and red wine for a larger batch; kept the filed version. The vegetables are chopped raw into the pan as the recipe asks, so the soffritto base is not used here. 300 ml broth is 1.25 servings of the 1 cup brodo. 6 servings, each enough for one plate of tagliatelle.

recipes.name: Ragù Napoletano
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, sweet and velvety, tomato cooked down for hours around whole pieces of beef and pork until it is almost jammy.
recipes.healthBenefit: The meat brings protein, iron and zinc and the long cooked tomato brings lycopene; it is a rich Sunday dish, with the meat eaten as a second course.

ingredients.cutPrep: in two or three large pieces
ingredients.prepNote: Neapolitans use a muscle cut such as gamboncello

instructions: Warm the oil in a deep heavy pot over medium heat and brown the beef, ribs and sausages on all sides, 10 to 15 minutes; set them aside.
Lower the heat, add the onion and cook it slowly for 15 to 20 minutes until soft and golden, stirring so it does not catch.
Return the meat, pour in the wine and let it evaporate for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the passata and salt, and bring to a simmer.

Set the lid ajar and cook on the lowest heat, the sauce barely blipping ("pippiare", as Naples says), for at least 6 hours, stirring every 20 to 30 minutes and adding a splash of water if it thickens too fast.
Add the basil at the end. Serve the sauce over ziti or rigatoni, and the meat after as a second course.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pork ribs and sausage.
From the long cooked tomato, eaten with the fat.

recipes.curationNote: Misya: 600 g beef muscle, 2 pork ribs, 500 g pork, onion, red wine, 2 l passata, paste, at least 6 hours. Cookist: passata, brisket, pork ribs, sausages, pork rind and braciole, onion, red wine, about 6 hours. Kept beef, ribs and sausage with 2 l passata, and left out the braciole and cotica, which are separate preparations. Serves 8 with pasta, the meat counted in the total because it is eaten as the second course.

recipes.name: Pesto alla Genovese
recipes.flavorProfile: Fragrant, green and creamy, sweet basil and pine nut softened by two cheeses and a fruity Ligurian oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Olive oil and pine nuts give mostly unsaturated fat, the cheeses bring calcium, and the raw basil adds vitamin K; it is rich, so a few spoonfuls dress a plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: young Genovese basil leaves, washed and dried
clove, or two for a stronger pesto
finely grated, aged 24 months or more

instructions: Crush the garlic with the pine nuts in a marble mortar until creamy.
Add the coarse salt and the basil a handful at a time, grinding with a rotating movement of the pestle against the walls rather than pounding, until the leaves give a bright green liquid.
Work in the two cheeses.
Pour in the oil in a thin stream, stirring with the pestle, until smooth.
Use it raw: loosen it with a spoonful of the pasta cooking water and toss with the pasta off the heat. Kept under a film of oil, it holds 2 to 3 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil and pine nuts.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Original pesto genovese
Scatti di Gusto, Pesto al mortaio: la ricetta di Roberto Panizza

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy gives 50 g basil, 120 ml oil, 70 g Parmigiano, 30 g Fiore Sardo, 1 to 2 garlic cloves, 15 g pine nuts and coarse salt. Roberto Panizza (Pesto World Championship) gives the mortar order: garlic with pine nuts, salt, basil worked with a rotating motion, cheeses, oil. About 290 g, 6 servings of 3 tbsp. curated_sauce_simple_pesto is the quick blender version; this one is the mortar original.

recipes.name: Besciamella
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, creamy and mild, with a soft warmth of nutmeg, the binding layer of every baked pasta.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk gives calcium and protein; it is made with butter and flour, so it is a rich sauce best used in the thin layers lasagne asks for.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

instructions: Warm the milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
In another pan melt the butter over low heat, add the flour all at once and stir for 1 to 2 minutes to cook the roux without letting it colour.
Take the pan off the heat and pour in a little warm milk, whisking hard to keep it smooth, then add the rest little by little.
Return to medium low heat and whisk until it boils and thickens, then cook 5 to 10 minutes more, stirring all the time.
Season with salt and nutmeg. If not using at once, press cling film onto the surface so no skin forms.
recipes.curationNote: Misya gives 500 ml milk, 50 g butter, 50 g flour, salt and nutmeg, and in the guide the ratio of 100 g each of butter and flour per litre of warm milk. Kept the litre batch, which is what a lasagne alla bolognese takes. About 1 litre, 8 servings of half a cup.

recipes.name: Salsa Verde
recipes.flavorProfile: Sharp, green and savoury, parsley and vinegar lifted by capers and anchovy, made to cut through boiled meats.
recipes.healthBenefit: Parsley brings vitamin K and vitamin C, the anchovies a little omega 3 fat, and olive oil makes up most of the rest.

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: one slice of crumb, crust removed
three salted fillets, rinsed and boned

ingredients.prepNote: optional; some Piedmontese leave it out

instructions: Soak the bread crumb in the vinegar for 5 to 10 minutes, then squeeze it lightly.
Chop the parsley finely with a knife, then chop in the anchovies, capers, garlic and the squeezed bread.
Mash in the hard-boiled yolks with a fork.
Stir in the oil a little at a time and season with salt and pepper.
Rest it 1 to 2 hours so the flavours settle. Serve with bollito misto, boiled tongue or eggs; it keeps 2 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the large amount of parsley.

citations.source: Dissapore, Bagnet verd o salsa verde piemontese

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore: 100 g parsley, a spoon of capers, anchovy, one slice of bread crumb soaked in 5 tbsp white vinegar, 2 hard-boiled yolks, 80 g oil, salt and pepper; garlic optional. Used whole anchovy fillets in place of paste, since the database holds the fish. About 250 g, 8 servings of 2 tbsp. Only one source could be opened for this sauce; the others tried were blocked.

recipes.name: Soffritto
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet and savoury, onion, carrot and celery melted slowly in olive oil into the quiet start of countless dishes.
recipes.healthBenefit: Onion, carrot and celery bring fibre, potassium and beta carotene, cooked gently in olive oil rather than fried hard.

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in a 1 to 3 mm dice
peeled, cut in a 1 to 3 mm dice
strings pulled, cut in a 1 to 3 mm dice

ingredients.prepNote: butter is used in the north
a pinch, to draw out the water

instructions: Cut the onion, carrot and celery into a very fine dice of 1 to 3 mm, all about the same size so they cook evenly.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over low heat, add the vegetables and the pinch of salt.
Cook gently for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until soft, translucent and sweet; it should never brown.
Use at once as the start of a soup, sauce or braise, or cool it and freeze it in 2 tbsp portions for up to 4 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrot, taken up better cooked in oil.
From the onion, carrot and celery.

citations.source: Ricette dal Mondo, Come fare il soffritto

recipes.curationNote: Cookist uses equal numbers of onion, carrot and celery in a 1 to 3 mm brunoise, cooked over low heat in oil or butter, and freezes it for 4 months. Ricette dal Mondo uses one of each for four people and about 10 minutes over low heat, never darkened. Weighted toward onion, as most Italian cooks do (two parts onion to one each of carrot and celery). About 300 g cooked, 10 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Ricotta Fatta in Casa
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, milky and slightly sweet, with a fine moist curd far fresher than any tub.
recipes.healthBenefit: A fresh cheese with protein and calcium from whole milk, lighter in salt than aged cheeses.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
ingredients.cutPrep: fresh whole milk, not ultra pasteurised
juice of about half a lemon, strained
ingredients.prepNote: Misya uses a whole lemon for a firmer curd

instructions: Pour the milk into a heavy pan with the salt and heat it over medium low heat, stirring now and then, to 185 to 195°F (85 to 90°C), when small bubbles form at the edge.
Take it off the heat, pour in the lemon juice and stir once or twice, gently.
Leave it untouched for 10 to 15 minutes while the curds separate from the greenish whey.
Line a sieve with damp cheesecloth, ladle in the curds and drain for 1 to 2 hours, longer for a firmer ricotta.
Keep it covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

citations.source: Cookist, Ricotta fatta in casa: la ricetta
Misya, Come fare la ricotta in casa

recipes.curationNote: Cookist: 2 l whole milk, half a lemon, salt, heated to 85 to 90°C, 10 minutes rest, 2 hours draining, about 500 g. Misya: 2 l milk with a whole lemon, about 400 g. This is the home acid-set ricotta; the dairy kind is cooked from whey after cheesemaking, which a home kitchen rarely has. About 450 g, 8 servings of a quarter cup. The nutrient total counts all 2 litres of milk, while much of the lactose and some protein leave with the whey, so it reads a little high.

recipes.name: Pangrattato Tostato
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, golden and toasty, a crunchy sand of bread and olive oil scattered over pasta in place of cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: It turns stale bread into a topping, giving crunch and a little carbohydrate with olive oil fat; a spoonful goes a long way.

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: stale country bread, crust and crumb, grated into coarse crumbs

instructions: Grate the stale bread on the coarse side of a box grater, or pulse it in a food processor to coarse crumbs.
Warm the oil in a wide frying pan over medium low heat and add the crumbs and salt.
Stir all the time for 5 to 8 minutes until they turn evenly golden brown and smell of toast, like dry sand; they darken fast at the end.
Tip them onto a plate to cool so they stop cooking. They keep crisp in a jar for a week.

citations.source: BlogSicilia, Muddica atturrata, il parmigiano dei poveri

recipes.curationNote: BlogSicilia describes muddica atturrata, breadcrumbs toasted in olive oil until golden like sand, the parmigiano of the poor, with garlic or anchovy as optional additions. Kept it plain so pasta con le sarde and other dishes can add their own. The food database has no breadcrumb row, so the stale country bread they are grated from is listed. About 150 g, 10 servings of 2 tbsp. One source opened; others were blocked.

recipes.name: Giardiniera
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy, tangy and bright, a jar of mixed vegetables in sweet and sour vinegar that wakes up boiled meats and antipasti.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lightly blanched vegetables keep much of their fibre and some vitamin C; the brine is mostly drained off, though it adds some salt.

ingredients.cutPrep: small white onions, peeled, or larger ones quartered

instructions: Bring the water, vinegar, salt and sugar to a boil in a large pot with the bay leaves and peppercorns.

Blanch the vegetables in the boiling brine in batches by firmness, about 2 minutes each: onions and carrots first, then cauliflower and celery, then peppers and green beans, lifting each batch out with a slotted spoon while still crisp.
Pack the vegetables into clean sterilised jars, mixing the colours, with a bay leaf in each.
Pour the hot brine over to cover by 1 cm (half an inch), leaving 1 cm of headspace, and seal.
Process the jars in boiling water for 20 minutes, cool them in the water, and check every lid has sealed.
Store in a cool dark place for 3 to 4 weeks before opening; once open, keep in the fridge and use within 2 weeks.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cauliflower, carrots, beans and peppers.
From the peppers and cauliflower, partly kept by the short blanching.
From the salted brine, which is drained before eating.

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: red and yellow pepper, 3 carrots, 2 celery ribs, half a cauliflower, 3 onions, 100 g green beans, brine of 1 l water and 1 l white wine vinegar with 25 g salt, 20 g sugar, bay and peppercorns, blanched in stages, pasteurised 20 minutes, rested 3 to 4 weeks. Cookist uses a wine and vinegar brine with more sugar and adds cucumber, radish and fennel. Kept the Recipes from Italy version. About 1.5 kg of vegetables, 16 servings of half a cup. The whole brine is counted in the total, though most is left in the jar.

recipes.name: Olio Santo (Chili Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fiery, fruity and warming, olive oil steeped red with dried Calabrian chili, a few drops at the table.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly extra virgin olive oil, with capsaicin from the chili; used by the drop, it adds heat with very little else.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 10 whole dried chilies, cut in rings with scissors

instructions: Make sure the chilies are completely dry, then snip them into rings with scissors, seeds and all, into a clean dry bottle.
Pour the oil over to cover them fully and close the bottle.
Leave it in a cool dark place for at least a week, shaking it now and then; it is at its best after about 30 days.
Once opened, keep it in the fridge and use it within a few months. Leave out fresh chili and raw garlic, which bring water into the oil and can let botulism grow.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.curationNote: Cookist: 10 dried chilies cut with scissors and covered with extra virgin oil, a week of steeping, best after 30 days, kept cold after opening. Misya adds fresh chili and garlic. Kept dried chili only: fresh chili and garlic in oil at room temperature carry a botulism risk, and the instructions say why. 250 ml is about 50 teaspoons, so a serving is a third of a tablespoon, the teaspoon or so it is used by.

recipes.name: Gremolata
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh, sharp and aromatic, parsley, lemon zest and raw garlic that lift a rich braise in the last minute.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw parsley and lemon zest bring vitamin C and vitamin K, scattered over the dish uncooked.

ingredients.cutPrep: flat leaf, a small bunch, leaves only
finely grated zest of half an untreated lemon, no white pith

instructions: Grate the zest of half a lemon, taking only the yellow skin.
Chop the parsley and garlic very finely together on a board.
Mix in the zest and chop a few strokes more so it all comes together.
Scatter it over ossobuco or another braise just before serving; it is best made within the hour.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw parsley and lemon zest.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Traditional osso buco

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy finishes ossobuco alla milanese with a bunch of parsley, the zest of half a lemon and a garlic clove, chopped and mixed. Veg|Citron, zeste, cru is the French table row for lemon zest (citron is lemon in French). About 4 tbsp, 4 servings, enough for four ossobuco. One source opened.

recipes.name: Polenta
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, warm and gently sweet, golden cornmeal stirred slowly into a smooth porridge that firms as it cools.
recipes.healthBenefit: A naturally gluten free whole grain dish that gives steady carbohydrate, with carotenoids from yellow maize.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot, or a copper paiolo, and add the salt.
Pour in the cornmeal in a thin rain, whisking all the time so no lumps form.
Lower the heat to a gentle bubble and switch to a long wooden spoon.
Cook for 40 to 60 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes and scraping the bottom, until it comes away from the sides of the pot.
Serve it soft from the pot, or pour it onto a board, let it set and cut it with string into slices to grill or fry.

nutritionHighlights.note: Lutein and zeaxanthin from yellow maize.

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: 400 g medium coarse cornmeal, 1.5 l water, 1 tbsp coarse salt, 40 to 60 minutes stirred every 5 to 10 minutes, 4 servings. Used 1.6 l for a slightly softer polenta. This is the plain base; curated_side_creamy_polenta is the creamy side finished with butter and cheese. Typed as a side because it is eaten on the plate.

recipes.name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, smoky toast rubbed with garlic under cool, juicy tomato, basil and green olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ripe tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene, and the extra virgin olive oil brings monounsaturated fat, on plain country bread.

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: 8 slices about 1 to 2 cm thick, a day old is best
ripe, seeded and cut in small dice

instructions: Mix the diced tomatoes with the basil, oregano, salt, pepper and about two thirds of the oil.
Leave the topping to rest for 30 to 60 minutes so the tomatoes give up their juice and take on the oil.
Toast the bread under a hot grill or in an oven at 375 to 400°F (190 to 200°C) for 5 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp outside but still soft in the middle.
Rub one side of each hot slice with the cut garlic and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Spoon the tomatoes on just before serving so the bread stays crisp.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomatoes, taken up better with the olive oil.
From the extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: 8 slices of 1 cm bread, 500 g tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, 10 basil leaves, 80 ml oil, topping rested about 1 hour, toasted at 200°C. Cookist: 2 cm country bread toasted at 190°C, 500 g datterini, dried oregano, one garlic clove, topping chilled 30 minutes. Kept both: plain tomato, garlic rubbed on the toast, basil, optional oregano. Bread weight is about 40 g a slice.

recipes.name: Insalata Caprese
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, milky mozzarella and sweet ripe tomato in alternating slices, with basil and a thread of fruity oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mozzarella brings protein and calcium and tomatoes bring vitamin C; it is a fairly rich plate because of the cheese.

ingredients.cutPrep: buffalo mozzarella if possible, sliced 1 cm thick and drained
ripe salad tomatoes, sliced 1 cm thick

instructions: Slice the tomatoes 1 cm thick, salt them lightly and leave them 2 to 5 minutes to give up some water.
Slice the mozzarella 1 cm thick and let it drain on a board for a few minutes.
Lay tomato and mozzarella slices overlapping on a plate, tucking a basil leaf between them.
Season with the rest of the salt and the oregano if using, pour over the oil and serve at cool room temperature, not straight from the fridge.
recipes.curationNote: Misya: 500 g buffalo mozzarella, 400 g tomatoes, basil, salt, oregano, oil, 1 cm slices, an hour in the fridge. Recipes from Italy: 4 tomatoes, 500 g mozzarella, 10 basil leaves, 4 tbsp oil, tomatoes salted 2 minutes. No balsamic, as neither source uses it. The database has no buffalo mozzarella, so plain mozzarella is counted.

recipes.name: Vitello Tonnato
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, cool slices of tender veal under a smooth, savoury tuna and caper sauce with a little tang.
recipes.healthBenefit: A protein-rich plate from lean veal, tuna and egg, with omega 3 fats from the tuna and anchovies; the sauce makes it fairly rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: one piece of girello (eye of round), trimmed and tied

ingredients.prepNote: the broth is mostly left over; a little goes in the sauce

ingredients.cutPrep: drained, plus a few for the top

instructions: Put the veal in a pot with the carrot, celery, onion, bay, cloves, peppercorns, wine and water, and bring it slowly to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 40 to 60 minutes, until the centre of the meat reads 145 to 150°F (63 to 65°C); the meat should stay pink and tender.
Let the veal cool completely in its broth, then lift it out and strain the broth.
Blend the egg yolks and whites, tuna, anchovies, capers and oil with about 150 ml of the broth until smooth and pourable like thick cream.
Slice the veal as thin as you can, lay the slices on a plate and cover them with the sauce.
Scatter a few capers over, cover and chill for at least 1 hour, or overnight, before serving cool.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the veal, tuna and eggs.
From the veal, fish and eggs.

recipes.curationNote: Misya: 1 kg girello simmered 1.5 hours with carrot, onion, celery, white wine; sauce of 3 eggs, 120 g tuna, capers, broth. Recipes from Italy: 800 g eye of round, wine, 1.5 L water, bay, cloves, peppercorns, 40 to 45 minutes to no more than 65°C; sauce of 2 hard-boiled eggs, 100 g tuna, 4 anchovies, 5 g capers, 150 ml broth. The older Piedmontese way, a sauce of eggs and tuna without mayonnaise, as both sources do. The whole broth water is counted though most of it is kept for another use, so it adds little but minerals.

recipes.name: Arancini
recipes.flavorProfile: A golden, crunchy shell around saffron rice with a hot heart of meat ragù, peas and melting cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: A filling treat with protein from the meat and cheese and some fibre from the peas; it is fried, so it is rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: threads, steeped in a little hot water

ingredients.name: caciocavallo cheese
ingredients.prepNote: provola or mozzarella can stand in

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: dried and ground to fine breadcrumbs
ingredients.prepNote: the database has no breadcrumbs, so dry country bread is counted
the absorbed share of about 1.5 litres of frying oil

instructions: Bring the salted water to the boil, add the rice and cook it, stirring now and then, for 15 to 18 minutes until it has taken up all the water.
Off the heat stir in the saffron with its water, the butter and the Parmigiano, then spread the rice on a tray and chill it for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until firm.
For the ragù, soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 5 to 8 minutes, add the pork and beef and brown them, then pour in the wine and let it bubble off.
Add the passata and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, adding the peas for the last 10 minutes, until thick; cool it completely.
With wet hands, flatten a handful of rice (about 120 g) in your palm, put a spoon of ragù and a few cubes of caciocavallo in the middle and close the rice around it into a ball or a cone.
Whisk the flour and water into a smooth batter, dip each arancino in it, then roll it in the breadcrumbs.
Fry 2 or 3 at a time in oil at 340 to 350°F (170 to 175°C) for 2 to 4 minutes, until deep gold; drain on paper and rest 5 minutes before eating.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, beef and cheeses.
From the peas and vegetables in the ragù.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Arancini (Sicilian Rice Balls)

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: 500 g rice in 1.2 L water with saffron, butter, 100 g Parmigiano, chilled 2 hours; ragù of pork, beef, wine, passata and peas; caciocavallo; flour and water batter and breadcrumbs; fried at 175°C. Misya: half the rice, the same ragù and caciocavallo, egg instead of batter. Kept the Palermo arancina al ragù with the flour batter (pastella) of the first source. Frying oil is counted as the absorbed share only.

recipes.name: Supplì
recipes.flavorProfile: A crisp oval of tomato rice that pulls apart into long strings of hot mozzarella, the telephone wire of its Roman nickname.
recipes.healthBenefit: A treat with protein from the veal, eggs and cheese and lycopene from the tomato; it is fried, so eat it as a snack.

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: dried and ground to fine breadcrumbs
ingredients.prepNote: the database has no breadcrumbs, so dry country bread is counted
the absorbed share of about 1.5 litres of frying oil

instructions: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, add the veal and brown it, then pour in the wine and let it bubble off.
Add the passata and a pinch of salt and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, until it is a loose meat sauce.
Stir in the rice and cook it in the sauce like a risotto for 16 to 18 minutes, adding hot stock a ladle at a time, until just tender and thick.
Off the heat beat in the Parmigiano, spread the rice on a tray and chill it for at least 30 minutes, longer if you can, until firm.
Take a spoonful of rice (about 50 g), press a baton of mozzarella into the middle and close it into an oval the length of a finger.
Roll each one in the beaten egg, then in breadcrumbs; repeat egg and crumbs once more for a sealed crust.
Fry a few at a time in oil at 350 to 360°F (175 to 180°C) for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep gold; drain and eat hot, so the cheese stretches.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the veal, egg, mozzarella and Parmigiano.

recipes.curationNote: Misya: 250 g rice cooked in a veal and tomato sauce with 400 ml vegetable broth, 150 g mozzarella, butter, parmesan, egg and breadcrumbs, 20 pieces. Cookist: 300 g rice, 250 g passata, 150 g mozzarella, 30 g Parmigiano, hot vegetable broth, a double coat of 3 eggs and breadcrumbs, fried at 180°C. Kept the Roman version with a little meat in the sauce (classic in Roman friggitorie) and the double coating. The broth points at the shared vegetable stock, 400 ml being about 1.75 cups.

recipes.name: Carpaccio di Manzo
recipes.flavorProfile: Paper-thin raw beef, cool and silky, crossed with a pale, tangy mayonnaise sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean beef brings protein, iron and vitamin B12; it is eaten raw, so only very fresh, well handled beef should be used and it is not for pregnancy or a weak immune system.

ingredients.cutPrep: very fresh, trimmed of all fat and sinew, never frozen

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Wrap the beef tightly in film and chill it for 1 to 2 hours so it is firm enough to slice.
Slice it as thin as possible with a very sharp knife, then lay each slice between sheets of baking paper and press it thinner with the flat of a knife.
Arrange the slices in one layer to cover cold plates, season lightly with salt and keep them chilled.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce and white pepper, then add milk a spoonful at a time until it just coats the back of a spoon.
Just before serving, drizzle the sauce over the beef in thin crossing lines and eat at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: Haem iron from the beef, well absorbed.

recipes.curationNote: The Harry's Bar original from Cookist: about 600 g of trimmed young beef sirloin, not frozen, sauced with 250 g mayonnaise, 1 tsp lemon, 1 to 2 tsp Worcestershire, 30 to 45 ml milk and white pepper; Giuseppe Cipriani created it in 1950 for Countess Amalia Nani Mocenigo. The second Cookist page is the common later version with arugula, Parmigiano shavings, lemon and oil, marinated no more than 10 minutes. Wrote the original, since it is the dish as Venice made it. The raw beef caution is in the health line.

recipes.name: Caponata
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft fried eggplant in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with celery crunch, salty olives and capers, best a day later.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggplant, celery, tomato and olives bring fibre and plant compounds; the eggplant is fried, so it carries a fair amount of oil.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 3 large, cut in 2 cm cubes, salted 30 minutes and patted dry

ingredients.prepNote: for salting the eggplant and to season
the absorbed share of the oil for frying the eggplant

ingredients.cutPrep: stalks, cut in 1 cm pieces, blanched 5 minutes

ingredients.prepNote: optional, as Recipes from Italy does

instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes, then squeeze gently and pat dry.
Fry them in batches in hot oil at 340 to 350°F (170 to 175°C) for 4 to 6 minutes until golden and soft, then drain on paper.
In a wide pan, soften the onion in the olive oil for 8 to 10 minutes, add the blanched celery, olives, capers and pine nuts and cook 5 minutes more.
Stir in the passata and tomato paste and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the eggplant, fold it in gently and cook 5 minutes so it takes up the sauce.
Pour in the vinegar with the sugar dissolved in it, let it bubble 2 to 3 minutes to soften the sharp edge, then turn off the heat and add the basil.
Cool completely and rest it covered for several hours or overnight; serve at room temperature.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggplant, celery, onion and olives.
From the olive oil and pine nuts.

recipes.curationNote: Misya: 600 g eggplant, celery, onion, 80 g green olives, 25 g capers, tomato, paste, a spoon of sugar and a small cup of vinegar, for 4. Recipes from Italy: 3 large eggplants salted 30 minutes and fried in seed oil, onion, 2 celery stalks blanched 5 minutes, capers, 200 g olives, pine nuts, 150 ml passata, 60 ml white wine vinegar, 2 tsp sugar, rested overnight, for 6. Followed the Palermo style of the second (fried eggplant, blanched celery, pine nuts) with Misya's tomato paste. Frying oil is counted as the absorbed share only.

recipes.name: Olive all'Ascolana
recipes.flavorProfile: Big green olives stuffed with a soft, nutmeg-scented meat filling, crumbed and fried crisp, briny and rich in one bite.
recipes.healthBenefit: A fried treat with protein from three meats, eggs and Parmigiano, and fat from the olives; it is rich, so a few go a long way.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 40 large green olives in brine, ideally Ascolana tenera, rinsed

ingredients.prepNote: 1 for the filling, 2 for the coating

ingredients.cutPrep: grated zest of half a lemon

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached
Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: dried and ground to fine breadcrumbs
ingredients.prepNote: the database has no breadcrumbs, so dry country bread is counted
the absorbed share of about 1.5 litres of frying oil

instructions: Soften the carrot, onion and celery in the oil for 5 minutes, add the three meats and brown them over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Pour in the wine and cook gently for 20 to 30 minutes, until the wine has gone and the meat is tender, then cool it.
Grind or blend the meat very fine, then mix in 1 egg, the Parmigiano, nutmeg, clove, lemon zest and salt; chill the filling for 30 minutes.
Cut each olive in a spiral around the stone with a small knife so the flesh comes away in one strip.
Wrap the olive flesh around a small ball of filling, pressing it back into the shape of an olive.
Roll each olive in flour, then in the 2 beaten eggs, then in breadcrumbs.
Fry in batches at 340 to 350°F (170 to 175°C) for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden, and serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pork, chicken, eggs and Parmigiano.
From the olives and olive oil.
The brined olives make these salty, so the filling is salted lightly.

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: 700 g olives, 200 g beef, 200 g pork, 100 g chicken, soffritto, 150 ml white wine, egg, 60 g Parmigiano, nutmeg, lemon zest, flour, egg and breadcrumbs, fried at 170°C. Cookist: 1 kg olives, beef, pork and chicken in pieces cooked 30 to 40 minutes in wine then blended, 95 g Parmesan, nutmeg, lemon, a clove, filling chilled 30 minutes, fried at 170 to 175°C. Kept the three meats cooked in wine and then ground, as in Ascoli. Frying oil is counted as the absorbed share only.

recipes.name: Crostini di Fegatini
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm toasted Tuscan bread spread with a soft, deep, savoury chicken liver paste lifted by capers and anchovy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken livers are one of the richest food sources of vitamin A, iron, folate and vitamin B12; because liver is so high in vitamin A it is best eaten now and then, and avoided in pregnancy.

ingredients.cutPrep: trimmed of sinew and any green spots

ingredients.prepNote: a small red onion as Visit Tuscany uses

ingredients.name: vin santo
ingredients.prepNote: dry white wine can stand in

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne

instructions: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil with the bay leaf over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the livers, raise the heat and brown them for 3 to 5 minutes, then pour in the vin santo and let it bubble off.
Add a ladle of the broth and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes, adding a little more broth if it dries out.
Take out the bay leaf, add the capers and anchovies and chop everything finely on a board, or pulse it briefly, so it stays a little rough.
Return it to the pan, stir in the butter and parsley and warm it for 2 to 3 minutes until spreadable.
Toast the bread, dip one edge of each slice quickly in the hot broth if you like, spread with the liver while warm and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken livers, in large amounts.

recipes.curationNote: Visit Tuscany: carrot, celery, small red onion, oil, bay, 300 g livers, capers, anchovy paste and butter, cooked 10 plus 15 minutes and blended, for 8. Cookist: 400 g livers, 200 ml meat broth, 2 anchovies, parsley, capers, half a glass of vin santo, onion, Tuscan bread, for 4. Combined: the Tuscan tourism board soffritto and butter with Cookist's vin santo and broth. Broth points at the Brodo di Carne base, 200 ml being about 0.85 of its 1 cup servings. Bread is about 30 g a slice.

recipes.name: Frittata di Zucchine
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, tender egg cake full of soft sweet zucchini and nutty Parmigiano, good warm or at room temperature.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein, vitamin B12 and choline, and zucchini adds potassium and a little fibre.
instructions: Warm half the oil in a 22 to 24 cm nonstick pan and cook the onion and zucchini over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and lightly golden; season and cool a little.
Beat the eggs with the Parmigiano, basil, salt and pepper, then stir in the zucchini.
Heat the rest of the oil in the pan, pour in the mixture and cook over low heat, covered, for 7 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set and the top is almost firm.
Slide it onto a plate or lid, turn it back into the pan the other way up and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more.
Rest it 5 minutes and cut it in wedges; it is as good at room temperature.
recipes.curationNote: Misya: 4 eggs, 400 g zucchini in thin rounds, 2 tbsp parmigiano, basil, 5 minutes then flipped. Recipes from Italy: 8 eggs, 100 g Parmigiano, 22 cm pan, low heat covered 7 to 8 minutes, flipped on a lid, 5 minutes more. Took 6 eggs as the middle ground for 400 g of zucchini, and the covered low-heat method with a flip.

recipes.name: Fiori di Zucca Fritti
recipes.flavorProfile: Delicate squash blossoms in a light, crackling batter, opening to melted mozzarella and a salty hit of anchovy.
recipes.healthBenefit: A fried treat with protein and calcium from the mozzarella and a little vitamin A from the flowers; best eaten as an occasional starter.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 12 zucchini flowers, pistils removed, wiped clean
fiordilatte, cut in 12 batons and drained well

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: ice cold; sparkling water is traditional, and the database counts still mineral water

ingredients.prepNote: the absorbed share of about 1 litre of frying oil

instructions: Open each flower gently, pinch out the pistil and check for insects without washing them.
Tuck a baton of mozzarella and a piece of anchovy inside each, then twist the petal tips closed.
Whisk the flour with the ice cold water and salt into a smooth batter as thick as cream; keep it cold.

recipes.name: Minestrone

instructions: Soak the dried beans in plenty of cold water for 12 hours, then drain them.

recipes.name: Ribollita
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, spoon-standing Tuscan soup of white beans, cavolo nero and bread, boiled again until thick and velvety.

instructions: Soak the beans overnight, about 12 hours, then simmer them in the 3 litres of water with a rosemary sprig over medium low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours, until tender.

In a large pot, cook the onion, carrot and celery in 4 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, add the potatoes, thyme and rosemary and cook 3 minutes, then the tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add the cavolo nero, cabbage and chard, pour in about 2 litres of the bean water, cover and simmer over low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours, adding water if it gets too dry.
Stir in the bean purée and cook 10 minutes, then the whole beans for 10 minutes more; season with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Tortellini in Brodo

instructions: Brown the pork loin in the butter for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then let it cool.
Grind or pulse the loin, prosciutto and mortadella until fine, then work in the Parmigiano, egg and nutmeg to a soft paste; no salt is needed.
Roll the egg pasta very thin, about 0.6 mm, and cut it into squares of 3 to 4 cm, keeping the rest covered so it does not dry.
Put a small ball of filling in the middle of each square, fold it into a triangle, press to seal, then wrap it round your fingertip and pinch the two points together.
Leave the tortellini on a floured tray to dry for 30 to 60 minutes.
Bring the broth to the boil, drop in the tortellini and simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes, until tender.
Serve them in their broth, about 25 to a bowl, with grated Parmigiano at the table.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Aglio, Olio e Peperoncino
recipes.flavorProfile: Spaghetti slick with golden olive oil, sweet with softly fried garlic and lit up by chili and fresh parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Olive oil brings monounsaturated fat and garlic and parsley add flavour without salt or cheese; a light, plant only plate.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

instructions: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente, keeping a cup of the water.
While it cooks, warm the oil in a wide pan over low heat with the garlic and cook for 2 minutes, until it just turns pale gold. Do not let it brown.
Add the chili and cook 1 minute more, then add a splash of pasta water to stop the garlic cooking.
Drain the spaghetti into the pan and toss over medium heat for 1 minute with a little more pasta water, until the oil turns lightly creamy.
Toss in the parsley and serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil.
A little from the parsley and fresh chili.

recipes.name: Tagliatelle al Ragù
recipes.flavorProfile: Wide, tender ribbons of fresh egg pasta holding a slow, deep meat ragù, finished with nutty Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef and egg pasta bring protein, iron and B12, and Parmigiano adds calcium; a hearty plate, rich from the pancetta.

components.note: rolled about 1 mm and cut in ribbons 7 to 8 mm wide

instructions: Roll the egg pasta about 1 mm thick, let the sheet dry for 10 to 15 minutes, then roll it up loosely and cut ribbons 7 to 8 mm wide. Shake them out into nests.
Warm the ragù in a wide pan over low heat.
Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, until tender with a little bite.
Lift them into the ragù with a splash of the cooking water and toss gently for 1 minute.
Serve with Parmigiano at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pancetta, eggs and Parmigiano.
From the beef in the ragù.

citations.source: Ricette dal Mondo, Tagliatelle alla bolognese

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: tagliatelle of 200 g 00 flour, 200 g semolina and 4 eggs, ragù of 300 g beef and 150 g pancetta, soffritto, passata, wine, milk, 2 hours, fresh tagliatelle about 5 minutes, for 4. Ricette dal Mondo: 350 g egg tagliatelle, a larger ragù of beef, pork and pancetta, 2.5 hours. Ragù alla bolognese is served on tagliatelle in Bologna, never on spaghetti. recipes.name: Lasagne alla Bolognese
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin layers of fresh egg pasta stacked with meat ragù, creamy béchamel and Parmigiano, baked until the top is golden and the edges crisp.
recipes.healthBenefit: A festive, rich dish: beef brings protein, iron and B12, and the béchamel and Parmigiano bring calcium along with a good deal of fat.

components.note: rolled about 1 mm and cut into sheets

ingredients.prepNote: for the dish and the top

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a deep baking dish of about 9 x 13 inches (23 x 33 cm).
Roll the egg pasta about 1 mm thick and cut it into sheets to fit the dish.
Blanch the sheets a few at a time in salted boiling water with the oil for 30 seconds to 1 minute, then lay them flat on a damp cloth.
Spread a little béchamel and ragù over the bottom of the dish, then a layer of pasta.
Repeat ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano and pasta for at least 5 layers, finishing with ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano and dots of butter.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Let it rest for 10 to 30 minutes before cutting, so the layers hold.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pancetta, eggs, milk and Parmigiano.
From the béchamel milk and Parmigiano.
From the beef in the ragù.

recipes.name: Trofie al Pesto
recipes.flavorProfile: Short, twisted pasta with soft potato and green beans, all coated in fragrant, cheesy basil pesto.
recipes.healthBenefit: Basil, olive oil and pine nuts bring vitamin K and unsaturated fat, and the potato and beans add potassium and fibre; the cheese makes it fairly rich.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 small, peeled and cut in small cubes
trimmed and cut in short lengths

instructions: Bring the water to the boil and salt it.
Add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes, then the potatoes for 3 minutes more.
Add the trofie and cook until al dente, usually 10 to 12 minutes for dried trofie, keeping a cup of the water.
Loosen the pesto in a large bowl with 2 to 3 tablespoons of the hot cooking water.
Drain everything and toss it in the bowl with the pesto, off the heat, so the basil stays green. Serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potatoes and green beans.
From the olive oil and pine nuts.

recipes.name: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
recipes.flavorProfile: A punchy, salty tomato sauce with melted anchovy, black olives, capers and chili, clinging to every strand of spaghetti.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomatoes bring lycopene and vitamin C, and olives and olive oil bring unsaturated fat; anchovies, capers and olives make it a salty dish.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta
Tomatoes, canned products, whole, without salt

ingredients.cutPrep: black Gaeta olives, pitted and halved

instructions: Warm the oil in a wide pan over low heat with the garlic, anchovies and chili for 1 to 2 minutes, pressing the anchovies until they melt.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until thick. Taste before adding any salt.
Cook the spaghetti in lightly salted boiling water until al dente, keeping a little water.
Drain the pasta into the sauce and toss over the heat for 1 minute with a splash of pasta water.
Scatter with parsley and serve. No cheese goes on it.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the olives and olive oil.
Anchovies, capers and olives are salty, so the pasta water is salted lightly.

recipes.name: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.flavorProfile: Rigatoni in a sweet, basil scented tomato sauce with soft, golden fried eggplant and salty shavings of ricotta salata.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggplant and tomatoes bring fibre, potassium and lycopene; frying the eggplant adds a fair amount of oil, so it is a fuller plate.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 large, sliced 5 mm thick, salted 30 minutes and patted dry

ingredients.prepNote: only what the eggplant absorbs is counted; fry in about 500 ml
or the same weight of peeled tomatoes
part for the eggplant, part for the pasta water

instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes, then pat them dry.
Heat the seed oil to about 350°F (175°C) and fry the slices in batches for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden. Drain on paper.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic in a pan for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 20 minutes.
Pass the sauce through a food mill, discard the garlic, add half the basil and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more, until thick.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, drain and toss it with the sauce and half the eggplant, cut in strips.
Serve topped with the rest of the eggplant, the ricotta salata and the last basil leaves.

recipes.name: Spaghetti alle Vongole
recipes.flavorProfile: Spaghetti finished in the briny juices of fresh clams with garlic, white wine, a little chili and lots of parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Clams are a good source of protein, iron and vitamin B12, and the sauce is mostly olive oil and clam juice rather than cream or cheese.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.cutPrep: about 1.2 kg (2.6 lb) clams in the shell, which gives about 180 g of meat
ingredients.prepNote: the meat weight is counted, not the shells
part for purging the clams, part for the pasta water

instructions: Purge the clams in cold salted water for 30 minutes to 2 hours, then rinse them and throw away any that are broken or stay open when tapped.
Warm 3 tablespoons of the oil in a wide pan with the garlic, chili and parsley stems, add the clams, cover and cook over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Lift out the clams and strain the juices through a fine sieve. Take most of the clams out of their shells, keeping a few whole.
Pour the wine and strained juices back into the pan and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti in lightly salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says and finish it in the pan for 2 minutes, tossing, until the sauce turns creamy.
Add the clams, the remaining oil and the chopped parsley, toss for 30 seconds and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: Clams are one of the richest sources.
From the clams and durum wheat pasta.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Spaghetti with Clams

recipes.name: Orecchiette con le Cime di Rapa
recipes.flavorProfile: Little ear shaped pasta cooked with tender, gently bitter broccoli rabe, tossed in olive oil with melted anchovy, garlic and chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Broccoli rabe brings vitamin K, vitamin C, folate and calcium, and the dish is dressed with olive oil rather than cheese.

components.note: shaped as orecchiette and dried on a floured cloth

ingredients.cutPrep: cime di rapa, tough stems and outer leaves removed, about 500 g trimmed

ingredients.prepNote: one large pot for pasta and greens

instructions: Shape the semolina dough: roll it into ropes about 1 cm thick, cut in pieces of 1 cm, drag each across the board with a round tipped knife so it curls, then turn it inside out over your thumb into a little ear.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over low heat with the garlic and chili for 2 to 3 minutes, add the anchovies and stir until they melt. Take it off the heat.
Bring the salted water to the boil and add the broccoli rabe and the fresh orecchiette together; cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until both are tender. Dried orecchiette go in 5 minutes before the greens.
Drain, keeping a cup of water, and tip it all into the pan.
Toss over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, gently so the leaves stay whole, adding a splash of water if dry.
Finish with a drizzle of raw olive oil and serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the greens and the anchovies.

recipes.name: Pasta al Forno
recipes.flavorProfile: Rigatoni baked with meat ragù, creamy béchamel and melting mozzarella under a golden crust of Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef, milk and cheese bring protein, calcium and B12; it is a rich, filling bake, so a plate with a green salad is plenty.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and butter a baking dish of about 8 x 12 inches (20 x 30 cm).
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water for half the packet time, so they finish in the oven, and drain them.
Toss the pasta with the ragù, two thirds of the béchamel, the mozzarella and half the Parmigiano.
Spread it in the dish, cover with the rest of the béchamel and scatter over the remaining Parmigiano.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, then turn the oven up to 400°F (200°C) for 5 minutes, until the top is golden.
Rest for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, milk, mozzarella and Parmigiano.

recipes.name: Ravioli Ricotta e Spinaci
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender egg pasta pillows filled with creamy ricotta and spinach, dressed in nutty brown butter with crisp sage and Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Spinach brings folate, vitamin K and iron, and ricotta and Parmigiano bring protein and calcium; the butter sauce makes it fairly rich.

ingredients.prepNote: part for the filling, most for the pasta water

instructions: Wilt the spinach in a covered pan with only the water left on its leaves for 3 to 4 minutes, cool it, squeeze it very dry and chop it finely.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, Parmigiano, egg, nutmeg, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Roll the pasta into thin sheets, dot teaspoons of filling 4 cm apart on one sheet, brush around them with a little water and lay a second sheet on top.
Press out the air around each mound, cut the ravioli with a wheel or cutter and lay them on a floured tray.
Melt the butter with the sage over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until it smells nutty and the leaves are crisp.
Cook the ravioli in salted, gently boiling water until they float, then 1 to 2 minutes more, and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Toss them in the sage butter with a spoonful of cooking water and serve with Parmigiano.

Recipes from Italy: 150 g 00 flour, 150 g semolina, 3 eggs; filling of 300 g ricotta, 400 g spinach, 5 to 6 tbsp Parmigiano, 1 egg, nutmeg; 70 g butter and sage; cooked until they float then 1 to 2 minutes, for 6. recipes.name: Tortellini
recipes.flavorProfile: Small rings of thin egg pasta filled with pork loin, prosciutto, mortadella and Parmigiano, tossed in melted butter with more Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: The meats, egg and Parmigiano bring protein and calcium; the cured meats and butter make it rich and salty, so portions are small.
instructions: Brown the pork loin in the butter for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then let it cool.
Grind or pulse the loin, prosciutto and mortadella until fine, then work in the Parmigiano, egg and nutmeg to a soft paste; no salt is needed.
Roll the egg pasta very thin, about 0.6 mm, and cut it into squares of 3 to 4 cm, keeping the rest covered.
Put a small ball of filling in the middle of each square, fold it into a triangle, press to seal, then wrap it round your fingertip and pinch the two points together.
Leave the tortellini on a floured tray to dry for 30 to 60 minutes.
Cook them in salted, gently boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, until tender, and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Toss them with the melted butter and a spoonful of cooking water, and serve with Parmigiano. For the dish in broth, see Tortellini in Brodo.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, cured meats, egg and Parmigiano.
The prosciutto, mortadella and cheese are salty.

recipes.name: Cannelloni
recipes.flavorProfile: Rolls of fresh egg pasta filled with ricotta and spinach, baked under tomato sauce and béchamel until bubbling and golden.
recipes.healthBenefit: Spinach brings folate, vitamin K and iron; ricotta, béchamel and Parmigiano bring protein and calcium, and the tomato sauce adds lycopene.

components.note: rolled about 1 mm and cut in 12 rectangles of 10 x 12 cm

ingredients.prepNote: part for the filling, part for the top
part for the filling, most for the blanching water

instructions: Heat the oven to 390°F (200°C) and butter a baking dish.
Wilt the spinach in a covered pan for 3 to 4 minutes, cool it, squeeze it dry and chop it finely.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, two thirds of the Parmigiano, the egg, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Blanch the pasta rectangles in salted boiling water for 1 minute and lay them flat on a damp cloth.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the dish. Pipe or spoon a line of filling along each rectangle, roll it up and lay it seam side down in the dish.
Spoon over the rest of the tomato sauce, then the béchamel, and scatter with the remaining Parmigiano.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden, and rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Pasta alla Genovese
recipes.flavorProfile: Ziti in a deep, sweet sauce of onions melted down for hours with beef and white wine, finished with Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein, iron, zinc and B12, and the long cooked onions bring fibre and flavour without tomato or cream.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.prepNote: a little for the sauce, most for the pasta water

instructions: Warm the oil in a heavy pot, add the carrot and celery and cook for 5 minutes over low heat.
Add the beef and brown it on all sides for 5 to 8 minutes, then add half the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Pile in the onions with the bay leaf, parsley and a pinch of salt, cover and cook over the lowest heat for about 2 hours, stirring now and then; the onions give off enough liquid to cook in.
Uncover, add the rest of the wine and cook for another 1 hour, until the onions have melted into a thick, amber sauce and the beef is tender. Add a splash of water if it catches.
Lift out the beef and keep it warm to serve as a second course, or shred some back into the sauce.
Cook the ziti in salted boiling water until al dente, drain and toss them with the onion sauce for 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve with pepper and Parmigiano if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the onions, carrot and celery.

recipes.name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
recipes.flavorProfile: Spaghetti in a smooth, sweet tomato sauce perfumed with garlic and fresh basil and finished with good olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cooked tomatoes with olive oil bring lycopene, vitamin C and potassium; a light, plant only plate.

Tomatoes, canned products, whole, without salt

ingredients.prepNote: a little for the sauce, most for the pasta water

instructions: Warm most of the oil in a wide pan with the garlic and a few basil leaves over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then uncover and cook 10 to 20 minutes more, until thick. Take out the garlic.
Blend or pass the sauce if you want it smooth.
Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente, keeping a little water.
Finish the spaghetti in the sauce over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes with a splash of pasta water.
Off the heat, toss in the torn basil and the raw oil and serve.
