recipes.name: Pasta con le Sarde
recipes.flavorProfile: Bucatini cooked in wild fennel water and tossed with fresh sardines, sweet onion, raisins, pine nuts and saffron, under crisp toasted breadcrumbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sardines are rich in omega-3 fats, vitamin D, B12 and calcium, and fennel, raisins and nuts add fibre and minerals.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.cutPrep: fresh, cleaned and butterflied, heads and bones removed
wild fennel fronds and tender stems
a pinch of threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water

ingredients.prepNote: for the fennel, then the pasta in the same water

instructions: Boil the wild fennel in the salted water for 10 minutes, lift it out, squeeze it and chop it. Keep the green water for the pasta.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, then melt the anchovies into it.
Add the sardines and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking them up with a wooden spoon.
Add the chopped fennel, drained raisins, pine nuts, almonds and the saffron with its water, and cook for 5 minutes, adding a ladle of fennel water to keep it saucy.
Bring the fennel water back to the boil and cook the bucatini until 2 minutes short of al dente.
Drain the pasta into the sauce and toss over the heat for 2 minutes with a splash of the water.
Serve topped with the toasted breadcrumbs, which take the place of cheese. Palermo also layers it in a dish and bakes it at 350°F (180°C) for 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Fettuccine al Burro
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh egg ribbons tossed with butter, Parmigiano and a little pasta water into a smooth, pale, nutty cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: Parmigiano brings protein and calcium; with butter as the sauce it is rich, so a small plate goes far.

components.note: rolled about 1 mm and cut in ribbons 6 mm wide

instructions: Roll the egg pasta about 1 mm thick, let the sheet dry for 10 minutes, then roll it loosely and cut ribbons about 6 mm wide.
Put the butter in a warm serving bowl or wide pan off the heat.
Cook the fettuccine in salted boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes, until tender.
Lift them into the butter with half a cup of the cooking water and toss until the butter melts.
Add the Parmigiano a handful at a time, tossing and adding a little more water, until it turns into a smooth cream that coats the pasta.
Serve at once, with pepper if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the Parmigiano and eggs in the pasta.
From the butter and cheese; a rich dish.

recipes.name: Agnolotti del Plin
recipes.flavorProfile: Tiny pinched parcels of thin egg pasta filled with roast pork, veal and greens, dressed in butter and sage.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and veal bring protein, B12 and zinc, the greens add vitamin K and folate, and Parmigiano adds calcium; the butter makes it rich.

components.note: rolled very thin, 1 mm or less

ingredients.prepNote: part for the filling, most for the pasta water

instructions: Brown the pork and veal in the oil with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and rosemary for 8 to 10 minutes, pour in the wine and cook covered over low heat for 40 to 60 minutes, until tender. Keep the cooking juices.
Boil the spinach, cabbage and escarole for 3 to 5 minutes, drain, squeeze dry.
Mince the meat, vegetables and greens finely, then mix in the egg, Parmigiano, nutmeg, salt and pepper to a firm paste.
Roll the pasta very thin and cut it in strips about 8 cm wide. Pipe or dot small balls of filling, about the size of a hazelnut, 2 cm apart along the middle.

Fold the pasta over the filling, then pinch it between each ball with thumb and finger (the plin), press along the edge and cut the strip into single parcels with a fluted wheel, rolling it so each closes.
Cook in salted, gently boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, until they rise and are tender.
Melt the butter with the sage until it smells nutty, toss the agnolotti in it with a spoonful of the roast juices, and serve with Parmigiano.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, veal, egg and Parmigiano.
From the spinach, savoy cabbage and escarole.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Agnolotti del plin piemontesi al canovaccio

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore: 300 g 00 flour and 3 eggs rested 30 minutes; filling of 200 g spinach, 200 g ground pork, 200 g ground veal, 1 egg, oil, onion, rosemary, garlic, bay, 50 g Parmigiano, browned, cooked with broth, chopped and bound; sheet 1 to 2 mm; 3 to 5 minutes; butter and sage plus roast juices. Scatti di Gusto: 200 g flour, 2 eggs; filling of 100 g pork loin, 100 g veal, 100 g rabbit roasted with carrot, celery, onion and white wine, 30 g savoy cabbage, 30 g escarole, 1 egg, 15 g cheese; served in a napkin or with roast juices. Rabbit is left out, since the only rabbit row in the database is wild rabbit, and the pork and veal are raised to cover it. Pasta points at Pasta Fresca all'Uovo (3 servings, 300 g flour and 3 eggs).

recipes.name: Busiate alla Trapanese
recipes.flavorProfile: Long spiral semolina pasta coated in a raw pesto of fresh tomato, almonds, basil and garlic, with a little Pecorino.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw tomatoes bring vitamin C and potassium, almonds bring vitamin E, magnesium and fibre, and the olive oil brings unsaturated fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: ripe, blanched 2 minutes, peeled and deseeded
clove, red garlic of Nubia if you can find it

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch for the pesto, most for the pasta water

instructions: Roll the semolina dough into thin ropes about 3 mm thick and cut them in lengths of 10 to 15 cm. Lay a skewer or knitting needle diagonally on each piece and roll it under your palm so the dough wraps round in a spiral, then slide it off. Leave the busiate to dry for 1 to 2 hours.
Pound the garlic with a pinch of salt in a mortar, then add the almonds and pound to a coarse crumb.
Add the basil and pound to a paste, then the tomatoes, and finally work in the oil and Pecorino. A food processor in short pulses also works.
Cook the busiate in salted boiling water for 4 to 6 minutes, until tender with a bite.
Drain them, keeping a little water, and toss with the raw pesto in a bowl, loosening with a spoonful of water. Do not heat the sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw tomatoes and basil.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Busiate alla trapanese

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore: 400 g re-milled semola, 200 ml water, rest 30 minutes, shaped on a skewer, dried 2 hours; 250 g cherry tomatoes blanched 2 minutes, peeled, deseeded; 50 g almonds boiled 3 minutes and skinned; 10 basil leaves; garlic; oil; salt; mortar; 50 g pecorino at the end. Scatti di Gusto: 400 g semola, 200 ml cold water, rest 60 minutes; 250 g pomodori perini, 50 g almonds, 50 g basil, 1 tbsp pecorino, red garlic, oil; pasta cooked about 5 minutes. Pasta points at Pasta di Semola (4 servings, 400 g semola).

recipes.name: Linguine allo Scoglio
recipes.flavorProfile: Linguine tossed with clams, mussels, squid and prawns in their sea juices, with cherry tomatoes, garlic, white wine, chili and parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shellfish bring lean protein, iron, zinc, iodine and plenty of vitamin B12, with olive oil and tomato rather than cream.

ingredients.baseName: Durum wheat, macaroni and spaghetti, dry pasta

ingredients.cutPrep: about 800 g clams in the shell, which gives about 120 g of meat
ingredients.prepNote: the meat weight is counted, not the shells

ingredients.cutPrep: about 800 g mussels in the shell, scrubbed and debearded, which gives about 200 g of meat
ingredients.prepNote: the meat weight is counted, not the shells

ingredients.cutPrep: prawns, shelled and deveined, a few left whole

ingredients.prepNote: part for purging the clams, part for the pasta water, lightly

instructions: Purge the clams in cold salted water for at least 30 minutes. Scrub and debeard the mussels. Throw away any shells that are broken or stay open when tapped.

Open the clams and mussels in a covered pan with a little oil and one garlic clove over high heat for 3 to 5 minutes, then discard any that stay shut. Strain and keep the juices, and shell about half.
Warm the rest of the oil with the other garlic clove and the chili in a wide pan, add the squid and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and the strained shellfish juices and cook for 5 minutes, then add the prawns for 2 minutes.
Cook the linguine in lightly salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says and finish them in the pan for 2 minutes, tossing.
Add the clams, mussels and parsley, toss for 30 seconds and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: Clams and mussels are among the richest sources.

citations.source: Recipes from Italy, Spaghetti allo Scoglio
Ricette dal Mondo, Spaghetti allo scoglio

recipes.curationNote: Recipes from Italy: 350 g pasta, 1 kg clams, 1 kg mussels, 300 g squid, 300 g shrimp, 200 g cherry tomatoes, chili, 2 garlic, 5 tbsp oil, 150 ml wine, parsley, for 4. Misya: 400 g spaghetti, 500 g clams, 6 scampi, 2 squid, 500 g mussels, 10 cherry tomatoes, garlic, half a glass of wine, clams purged at least 30 minutes, shellfish opened covered, liquor strained, for 6. Ricette dal Mondo: 350 g spaghetti, squid, scampi, prawns, mussels, clams, a glass of wine, 250 g cherry tomatoes, brandy, parsley, garlic. Brandy left out as only one of three uses it. Clams and mussels are counted by edible meat weight, since the database rows are for the meat.

recipes.name: Pici all'Aglione
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, hand-rolled Tuscan noodles in a sweet, mellow tomato sauce made with slowly cooked giant garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomatoes bring lycopene, vitamin C and potassium, and the garlic and olive oil bring flavour without cheese or meat; a plant only plate.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, all purpose, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: cloves of aglione, peeled and halved, green shoot removed
ingredients.prepNote: aglione is the large, mild garlic of the Val di Chiana; ordinary garlic, fewer cloves, also works

ingredients.baseName: Tomatoes, canned products, whole, without salt

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch for the dough and sauce, most for the pasta water

instructions: Knead the flour, lukewarm water, 1 tablespoon of oil and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough. Wrap it and rest it for 30 minutes to 1 hour.

Roll the dough about 1 cm thick and cut strips 1 cm wide. Roll each strip under your palms on an unfloured board into a long, thick noodle of about 3 to 4 mm, then lay it on semolina so it does not stick.
Put the garlic in a wide pan with the oil over the lowest heat and cook it for 15 to 20 minutes, until soft and pale, without browning. Mash it with a fork.
Add the tomatoes, the chili if using and a pinch of salt and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until thick. Stir in the vinegar at the end.
Cook the pici in salted boiling water for 4 to 6 minutes, until tender, keeping a little water.
Toss them in the sauce for 1 minute with a splash of the water and serve. In the Val di Chiana no cheese goes on top.

citations.source: Dissapore, Pici all'aglione, ricetta originale toscana

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore: 400 g type 0 flour, 200 ml lukewarm water, 1 tbsp oil, salt, rest 30 minutes to 4 hours, hand-rolled; sauce of 4 ripe tomatoes, 2 heads of aglione cooked very low and mashed, 5 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp white wine vinegar, 20 minutes; pici about 4 minutes; no cheese. Ricette dal Mondo: 350 g dried pici, 6 to 8 garlic, 600 g tomato pulp, 150 ml white wine, oil, a pinch of sugar, 10 to 15 minutes. Pici are flour and water without egg, so the dough is written here rather than pointing at a base. Aglione is not its own row in the database, so it is entered as garlic. The flour is listed as Boiled since it becomes the pici.
